review_notes: I read the whole file and checked its uses across Mathlib with Grep. I also read the one downstream use, in Flat.lean. The binary and pullback lemmas (`prod_eq_inf`, `coprod_eq_sup`, `pullback_eq_inf`, `pushout_eq_sup`) are already simp and have sensible orientation. The `@[simps]` cone definitions look fine. I found no loop or competing-rule problem. The only concern is that the complete-lattice versions (`limit_eq_iInf`, `colimit_eq_iSup`) are not simp, unlike the binary and pullback versions. Only one downstream user was found, so the evidence is modest. I could not run Lean, so I have not checked whether the proposed attribute interacts with other simp sets.

findings.excerpt: theorem limit_eq_iInf (F : J ⥤ α) : limit F = iInf F.obj :=
findings.problem: The binary, pullback and pushout identities in this file (`prod_eq_inf`, `coprod_eq_sup`, `pullback_eq_inf`, `pushout_eq_sup`) are `@[simp]`. Each rewrites a categorical limit to the lattice operation. The general complete-lattice identities `limit F = iInf F.obj` and `colimit F = iSup F.obj` are not simp. The same file therefore normalizes a binary limit to `⊓` but leaves `limit F` unchanged. The one downstream user, Flat.lean, has to pass `CompleteLattice.colimit_eq_iSup` by hand to `simp`/`simpa`. Its RHS is the lattice-native form, and the rewrite terminates, because the RHS has no `limit`/`colimit`.
findings.proposed_change: Mark both `limit_eq_iInf` and `colimit_eq_iSup` `@[simp]`, consistent with the sibling lemmas. Alternatively, keep them unannotated and state in the docstring that they are intentionally non-simp. Check the existing `simp [CompleteLattice.colimit_eq_iSup]` calls in Flat.lean (about lines 368 and 390) afterwards. The `Limits.CompleteLattice` namespace means the attribute only matters for callers who work in a lattice category.
findings.benefit: Lattice-valued diagrams would simplify to `iInf`/`iSup` in the same way as binary products and pullbacks. Users would not need to know and import these lemma names to get the canonical lattice form.
